state.misconception_label: Assumes that an arrow on a number line starts at zero

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: ![Number line with -12 and -7 marked. Starting at -12, follow an arrow pointing to the right labelled +10. Then there is an arrow labelled b pointing to the left, which ends at -7 on the number line.]() What is the value of \( b \) ? I got \( -7 \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think the arrow starting at -12 goes to +10? Can you explain your reasoning for how you arrived at the value of -7 for \( b \)?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I thought the arrow just moved from -12 to -7 directly, like it was just counting up. But now I'm not sure how the +10 fits in. Does that mean I need to add something to -12 first before I can figure out \( b \)?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think adding +10 is involved in finding the value of \( b \)? How does this relate to the misconception of assuming that an arrow on a number line starts at zero?
